name: Bitdefender
description: Romanian cybersecurity company selling consumer antivirus and internet-security suites (Total Security, Premium VPN and related products) direct to consumers worldwide.

evidence.summary: Bitdefender's own affiliate-partners page (fetched) routes join buttons to its Impact program and describes a base 20% revenue share for new customers, 50% on business products, with custom deals up to and beyond 100%. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Consumer security software is a core tech-creator niche with highly demonstrable products (scans, VPN, device protection).
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is run through Impact with creator-ready join links from the brand's own partner page; no separate ambassador page was found.
reasons.compensation: 20% revenue share base for new customers, 50% on business products and custom deals above 100% for top partners; no cap statement published, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Program details and join route are on the brand's own partner page; no public partnerships email was seen on the fetched page.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Impact from the brand's own page.
reasons.credibility: One of the largest consumer antivirus vendors globally, selling direct in many countries.

name: Malwarebytes
description: US cybersecurity company selling consumer anti-malware and privacy products (Premium Security, Privacy VPN and identity-theft protection) direct to consumers.

evidence.summary: Malwarebytes' own affiliates page (fetched) states affiliates earn up to 30% per sale through Cleverbridge Partnerize, with a 45-day referral period and commission paid within 30 days of the point of sale. Some third-party reviews claim up to 40% or a CJ route; the brand's own page governs. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Consumer anti-malware and privacy tools are a staple tech-creator niche with easy before/after demonstrations.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand runs a public affiliates page aimed at promoters; no separate creator or ambassador program page was found.
reasons.compensation: Up to 30% per sale (a ceiling, not a base rate) via Partnerize, 45-day referral period; no cap statement published, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Program terms and join route are published on the brand's own affiliates page; no public partnerships email was seen.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application from the brand's own affiliates page.
reasons.credibility: Long-established consumer security vendor with a large installed base.

name: ESET
description: Slovak cybersecurity company selling consumer internet-security products (NOD32 Antivirus, Internet Security and Smart Security Premium) in more than 200 countries.

evidence.summary: ESET's online-affiliates program is listed across multiple affiliate directories (getlasso, affpaying, openaffiliate.dev, Sovrn) with consistent terms: 20% recurring commission on CJ Affiliate, paid on new purchases AND renewals, 45-day cookie, $50 payout threshold, manual approval. The brand's own program page is eset.com/us/business/partner/online-affiliates. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Consumer antivirus is a proven tech-creator niche; ESET's lightweight products demo well on older hardware.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Program is marketed to publishers through CJ; no dedicated creator page was found on the brand's own site.
reasons.compensation: 20% recurring, and unusually it pays on renewals as well as new purchases, which compounds creator earnings; no cap statement published, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Contact runs through the CJ program and the brand's partner pages; no public partnerships email was seen.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application through CJ Affiliate with manual approval and a $50 payout threshold.
reasons.credibility: One of the oldest independent antivirus vendors, headquartered in Bratislava and selling in 200+ countries.

name: Norton
description: US consumer cyber-safety brand from Gen Digital selling antivirus, VPN and identity-protection subscriptions (Norton 360, Norton VPN, LifeLock) direct to consumers.

evidence.summary: Norton's affiliate presence runs through Impact (also CJ and regional networks). Published rates CONFLICT: baseline listings report about 20% (LinkClicky, getlasso), some networks report 25% (Affilorama), and the Impact 'Norton VPN Creator' campaign page itself states a 50% payout with a 60-day referral period. Because the sources conflict, commission_rate is recorded as null with the conflict documented here. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Norton is one of the most recognised consumer security brands, an easy fit for mainstream tech and family-safety creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Impact runs a dedicated 'Norton VPN Creator' campaign, a direct signal the brand recruits creators, not just coupon sites.
reasons.compensation: Rate could not be settled: published figures conflict (about 20% baseline, 25% on some networks, 50% on the Impact creator campaign), so the rate is recorded as null rather than guessed; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Contact runs through the network programs; no public partnerships email was seen on the pages reviewed.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Impact and CJ.
reasons.credibility: Flagship consumer brand of Gen Digital, among the largest cyber-safety companies in the world.

name: MacPaw
description: Ukrainian software company selling Mac utilities direct to consumers, including CleanMyMac, Gemini 2, ClearVPN, The Unarchiver and Encrypto.

evidence.summary: MacPaw's own affiliate page (macpaw.com/affiliate, corroborated by openaffiliate.dev and clickaffiliate.net, checked Oct 2026) describes an Impact program paying a 35% starting commission per sale with performance tiers above that, a 180-day cookie, monthly payouts and manual review. The page's 'sky's the limit' wording is vague marketing, NOT an explicit no-cap statement, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: CleanMyMac and the Mac utility suite are natural, demonstrable products for Apple-focused creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand maintains its own affiliate landing page aimed at promoters and reviewers, with creator-friendly assets via Impact.
reasons.compensation: 35% starting commission with performance tiers above it and an unusually long 180-day cookie; 'sky's the limit' is not an explicit no-cap statement, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Program page and Impact dashboard provide the contact route; no public partnerships email was seen.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application through Impact with manual review.
reasons.credibility: Well-known Mac software house; scored one point lower because its catalogue is Apple-only.

name: Descript
description: US software company selling an AI-powered audio and video editor used by creators and podcasters, with text-based editing, screen recording and AI voice tools.

evidence.summary: Descript's own affiliate terms (fetched in full) pay a FLAT $25 one-time bounty per new qualifying subscription (Creator/Pro plans, monthly or annual; new customers only; no renewals), with a 30-day purchase window, so commission_rate is null and the flat bounty is recorded here. The same terms CAP total annual commissions at $100,000 per affiliate, so the program is explicitly capped, not uncapped; the cap field records 'unknown' per directory convention with the $100k cap documented here. Program page: descript.com/affiliate, run on PartnerStack.

reasons.niche_fit: Descript is a tool creators themselves use daily, so it fits creator-audience content almost perfectly.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The affiliate program is aimed squarely at creators and podcasters who demo the editor in their own workflows.
reasons.compensation: Flat $25 one-time bounty per new qualifying subscription, no renewals, and the terms cap annual commissions at $100,000 per affiliate, so earnings are bounded; rate recorded as null because it is a flat bounty.
reasons.contact_access: Full public terms and a program page on the brand's own domain; no public partnerships email was seen.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through PartnerStack from the brand's program page.
reasons.credibility: Established, venture-backed creator-tools company with a large user base.

name: Hamilton Beach
description: US small-appliance brand selling coffee makers, slow cookers, blenders, food processors and countertop ovens through its own store and major retailers.

evidence.summary: Awin's own program announcement (fetched) states the Hamilton Beach program pays 6% commission (a portion of revenue) on completed sales within a 45-day cookie window, with in-house account management, and warns that not all applications are accepted. FlexOffers lists 5%; Awin's own announcement governs. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Everyday kitchen appliances are highly demonstrable home and food-creator content.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The Awin announcement targets quality content publishers; no separate creator page was found.
reasons.compensation: 6% of revenue is modest but the brand's low price points convert in volume; 45-day cookie; no cap statement published, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Awin's announcement names program contacts at the network; no public brand partnerships email was seen.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application through Awin, but the announcement says applications are selective and not all are accepted.
reasons.credibility: The #1 selling brand of small kitchen appliances in the US, per the program's own description.

name: Keurig
description: US beverage-system brand (Keurig Dr Pepper) selling single-serve coffee brewers, K-Cup pods and other drink makers direct to consumers.

evidence.summary: Lasso's Keurig program listing (fetched) states 8% per sale with a short 10-day cookie, and its join link routes to FlexOffers (publisherpro.flexoffers.com). Other published sources conflict, quoting figures from about 1% (Rakuten) to 2-4% and category-split rates, and some name Impact instead. Because the rate and network reports conflict, commission_rate is recorded as null and FlexOffers is recorded from the listing's actual join link. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Coffee brewers and pods are everyday, highly demonstrable home products with a built-in repeat-purchase story.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is promoted to coffee bloggers and reviewers through network listings; no dedicated creator page was found.
reasons.compensation: Published rates conflict (about 1% to 8% depending on source and network) and the cookie is only 10 days, so the rate is recorded as null rather than guessed; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Contact runs through the networks; no public partnerships email was seen on the pages fetched.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through FlexOffers and other networks carrying the program.
reasons.credibility: The dominant single-serve coffee brand in the US, owned by Keurig Dr Pepper.

name: Pawfit
description: UK pet-tech company selling GPS pet trackers (Pawfit 3 and Pawfit Lite) with activity monitoring, sold direct to consumers with a subscription plan.

evidence.summary: Pawfit runs its own Affiliate Programme at affiliate.pawfit.com: affiliates receive a unique discount code (customers save up to 10%) and earn up to 20% commission, paid quarterly after a 30-day cooling-off period; the program is open to influencers, retailers and businesses. Its terms (pawfit.com/en-us/legal_affiliate.html) limit commissionable items to the Pawfit 3 and Pawfit Lite trackers. 'Up to 20%' is a rate ceiling, not an uncapped statement; no earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: GPS trackers are demonstrable pet-tech with strong lost-pet storytelling for pet creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The programme explicitly welcomes influencers and gives them customer discount codes to share in content.
reasons.compensation: Up to 20% commission (a ceiling) on tracker sales, paid quarterly after a 30-day cooling-off period; no cap statement published, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Dedicated affiliate portal on the brand's own subdomain; no public partnerships email was seen.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open signup at the brand's own affiliate portal for influencers, retailers and businesses.
reasons.credibility: Smaller UK pet-tech brand; scored lower because the range is two trackers plus a subscription.

name: PawSafe
description: US pet-products brand designing everyday pet-care products (including its dog seat belt and other safety and care items) sold direct to consumers from Wilmington, Delaware.

evidence.summary: PawSafe's own affiliate program page (fetched) states affiliates sign up via GoAffPro, are approved within 1-2 business days, and earn 30% of revenue on every referred sale; the page welcomes blogs, social media, websites and email lists (coupon-finder sites excluded). No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Pet safety and care products are everyday, demonstrable items for dog-focused creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own page explicitly recruits social-media and video creators, not just bloggers, and supplies a custom link per affiliate.
reasons.compensation: 30% of revenue on every referred sale is one of the stronger pet rates found; no cap statement published, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Signup and management run through the GoAffPro portal linked from the brand's page; no public partnerships email was seen (a postal address in Wilmington, Delaware is published).
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application with approval in 1-2 business days per the brand's own page.
reasons.credibility: Smaller DTC pet brand; scored lower on limited public track record compared with national pet retailers.
